title: Apply AI? It’ll Cost You
content:
Europe wants researchers and businesses to apply AI. But what happens when using AI on material they already have lawful access to means another licence, another payment, or a contractual ban?

Today, leaders from across Europe meet for the Apply AI Summit, a milestone in the EU’s wider efforts to encourage stronger uptake of AI across industrial sectors in Europe. It offers an opportunity to take stock of progress and set out plans on a topic that Commission President von der Leyen identified as a key priority in her State of the Union speech in September.

When the Apply AI Strategy first came out last year, Knowledge Rights 21 (KR21) welcomed it, recognising the value of an approach focused on the specific needs of each sector, rather than blunter, cross-cutting tools such as copyright. An untargeted approach risks causing significant collateral damage, in particular for research, and is not guaranteed to achieve its goals given that most (copyright-relevant) training takes place outside Europe.

title: Diamond Open Access for Scholarly Books: Lessons from Croatia
content:
Blog post by Iva Melinščak Zlodi (*)

The possibilities for making research openly accessible, and for enabling authors to retain control over their rights, are closely connected to the scholarly publishing models that dominate in different countries. This connection matters most in countries where resources to cover article and book processing charges (APCs and BPCs) are limited, and where publishing agreements that cover Open Access (OA) fees offer only partial solutions. Croatia offers a useful example of how established non-commercial publishing traditions can support more equitable access to scholarly knowledge.

title: European Rights Retention Community of Practice – Twelfth Meeting
content:
When?

  • Date: 3 December 2026
  • Time: 12:00 CET

    • What?

    This Community of Practice is an online collaborative space designed to bring together professionals to discuss and tackle the challenges around rights retention strategies.

    Save Your Spot!

    Register now to secure your spot.

    The Webinar

    This 12th meeting of the community, organised by Knowledge Rights 21 (KR21) partner SPARC Europe, will focus on recommendations for implementing rights retention. The session explores what it means to put rights retention into practice, whether or not an institution already has a policy in place, and builds on the recommendations drafted by the Rights Retention in Practice task force, which supports institutions in implementing rights retention. A more collaborative format creates the space to exchange experiences, share practical examples, and discuss how these recommendations can be applied in different institutional contexts.

    Community members are then invited to share their own experiences, highlight ongoing challenges, and collaborate on practical solutions in an open discussion.
